w10_P4_000749: A rail-yard engineer wants to know the total force, in kilonewtons, that the yard's winch system must deliver at peak across every depot at once. The company operates 7 depots, each depot runs 4 sidings, and each siding has 12 identical loaded carts that all start moving at the same instant. Every cart has a mass of 150 kg, and the maintenance log also notes that each cart's bearings were greased at a temperature of 35 °C. The acceleration given to each cart, in m/s², is the larger of the two values a that satisfy a² - 6a + 8 = 0. Working from the force on a single cart, expressed in kilonewtons, find the peak force the whole system must supply, in kN.
w10_P4_000758: On a test bench, a technician drives a 161 000 g steel sled along a low-friction rail with a small electric motor. The sled's acceleration, in m/s², is the larger of the two numbers x for which x² - 3x + 2 = 0. A pre-tensioned spring assists the motor by providing 28 N of the push needed, while the motor's own internal drag costs an extra 1 N that it must overcome. The bench is 3.5 m long. The technician then builds 3 identical sleds driven together by one shared motor, and a common coupling adds a further 26 N of load. What total force, in N, must the shared motor supply?
w10_P4_000768: A mining company wants the final figure, in kilojoules, that will go on the certification sheet for one of its ore skips. That figure is defined as the skip's energy of motion at full speed, less 20 J lost during a brake-pad test, converted to kilojoules, and then increased by a 15 kJ safety allowance. The loaded skip has a mass of 37 000 g. Its full speed, in m/s, is numerically equal to the area under the curve y = 1·x² + 5·x between x = 1 and x = 4. What number, in kJ, goes on the certification sheet?
w10_P4_000772: A hydraulic stamping press at a factory uses a 28 000 g ram. On each stroke the ram reaches a speed, in m/s, equal to the smaller of the two roots of v² - 15v + 56 = 0. The ram's hydraulic line operates at a pressure of 210 bar. The press makes 8 strokes per part, a shift produces 3 parts, and the shop runs 5 shifts in a batch. Taking the ram's energy of motion at full speed on a single stroke, find the total energy of motion delivered over the whole batch, in kJ.
w10_P4_000775: A logistics firm is sizing the combined thrust, in kilonewtons, that a fleet of tugs must deliver during a 3-shift day. On each shift, 8 tugs pull loaded trolleys at the same time, and every tug must move one trolley of mass 173 kg. The acceleration required of each trolley, in m/s², equals the sum of the terms 2k - 1 for k running from 1 to 5. Starting from the force on one trolley, stated in kilonewtons, what total force in kN must the fleet deliver across the day?
w10_P4_000779: A bobsled test rig launches a 47 000 g sled along an ice track. The sled's launch speed, in m/s, is numerically equal to the area under the curve y = 4x² + 0·x from x = 1 to x = 2. After launch, a pneumatic booster adds 12 J to the sled's energy of motion. The rig performs 10 launches per session, 7 sessions per day, and the test campaign lasts 6 days. What is the total energy of motion, in J, delivered across the whole campaign?
w10_P4_000787: A workshop needs the rating, in kilonewtons, of a towing bracket that will pull 2 identical trailers at once. The bracket rating is set at twice the load from one trailer, after a 25 N allowance for hitch friction has been subtracted from that single-trailer load. Each trailer has a mass of 196 kg. The trailer must accelerate at a rate, in m/s², equal to the largest whole number that divides both 315 and 162 without remainder. What rating, in kN, should the bracket carry?
w10_P4_000792: An amusement-park engineer is preparing the total energy figure, in joules, for a bumper-car circuit. That figure combines the energy of motion of 9 identical cars at running speed, plus 29 J stored in the circuit's collision bumpers, plus another 12 J held in the cars' lighting capacitors. Each car has a mass of 18 kg. The running speed of each car, in m/s, is the larger of the two roots of v² - 5v + 4 = 0. What is the total energy figure, in J?
w10_P4_000800: A 53 000 g crash-test dummy is fired from a sled along a rail. Its speed in m/s equals the number of different ways to choose 4 sensors from a set of 7. The dummy's energy of motion at that speed is recorded in kilojoules. During the run, 7 kJ is absorbed by a crumple zone and a further 23 kJ is absorbed by the harness, and then a rebound spring returns 16 kJ to the dummy. How much energy, in kJ, does the dummy carry after the rebound?
w10_P4_000807: A laboratory cart of mass 58 kg glides along an air track at a speed, in m/s, equal to the greatest common divisor of 303 and 325. The air track is 2.4 m long. A small compressed spring on the cart then adds 25 J to its energy of motion. Converted to kilojoules, that energy is the figure for one cart on one run. The lab runs 7 carts per session and holds 7 sessions. What is the total energy of motion, in kJ, across all sessions?
w10_P4_000811: A robotics lab tracks the net energy change, in kilojoules, of a test cart's battery pack over a series of 8 identical runs. On each run the cart's regenerative brake feeds the battery the cart's full energy of motion, expressed in kilojoules; the onboard heater then draws 16 kJ from the pack, and the sensor array draws another 4 kJ. The cart has a mass of 2 000 g. Its top speed on each run, in m/s, is the larger of the two solutions of v² - 7v + 6 = 0. What is the net energy change of the battery pack, in kJ, over the 8 runs?
w10_P4_000816: A hobby-rocket club needs the net energy balance, in kilojoules, of a launch sled's power unit after one launch. That balance is the sled's energy of motion at launch, in kilojoules, plus 12 kJ recovered from the sled's brakes, minus 28 kJ consumed by the launch winch. The sled has a mass of 5 000 g. Its launch speed, in m/s, is 9 times the larger root of x² - 11x + 30 = 0. What is the net energy balance, in kJ?
w10_P4_000819: A cargo-drone company is estimating the total energy of motion, in joules, that its fleet expends on take-off during a busy stretch. The stretch covers 11 days, each with 4 delivery windows, and in every window 5 drones take off at the same speed. Each drone has a mass of 34 000 g and its rotors spin at 5 400 rpm. The drones' take-off speed, in m/s, is found by taking the slope of the curve y = 2x³ - 5x² at x = 3 and subtracting 17 from it. What is the fleet's total take-off energy of motion, in J?
w10_P4_000820: A conveyor at a bottling plant has to accelerate a crate of mass 159 kg. The controller sets the acceleration, in m/s², as follows: it starts with the number of ways to choose 4 bottles out of 8, adds 2, and then subtracts 3. The conveyor belt is 12 m long. In addition to the force required to accelerate the crate, the drive must overcome a constant 28 N of belt friction. What total force, in N, must the drive supply?
w10_P4_000822: A shipyard is booking the total energy of motion, in kilojoules, delivered by 8 identical test launches of a lifeboat. For each launch the lifeboat's energy of motion at release is recorded in kilojoules. The lifeboat has a mass of 53 kg. Its release speed, in m/s, is 6 times the smaller root of x² - 9x + 20 = 0. What is the total energy of motion, in kJ, for the 8 launches?
w10_P4_000823: A 168 kg mine cart is driven by an electric motor along a level track. The cart's acceleration, in m/s², is set by adding 6 and 3 and multiplying the result by 7. The track runs 480 m from the face to the shaft. Four such carts are coupled into a train, and the motor must supply the force that accelerates all 4 at that rate. On top of that, a headwind in the tunnel adds 18 N of drag, a tailwind section later removes 28 N, and a lubricated bend reduces the load by a further 17 N. What is the total force, in N, that the motor supplies?
w10_P4_000828: A safety inspector wants the energy, in joules, remaining in a runaway-cart arrester after a test. The arrester takes in the cart's full energy of motion, then loses 25 J to heat in the first friction pad, another 18 J in the second pad, and a further 28 J in the third pad. The cart has a mass of 44 kg and is 1.8 m long. Its speed, in m/s, when it hits the arrester equals the area under the curve y = 3x² + 1·x from x = 0 to x = 4. What energy, in J, remains in the arrester?
w10_P4_000833: A wind-tunnel team is preparing a final energy figure, in kilojoules, for a test carriage. The figure is computed from the carriage's energy of motion at test speed: 14 J is deducted for bearing losses, 25 J is added back from a flywheel, the result is converted to kilojoules, and then 1 kJ is subtracted as a calibration offset. The carriage has a mass of 10 000 g. Its test speed, in m/s, is equal to the area under the curve y = 2x² + 6x from x = 3 to x = 4. What is the final energy figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_000836: A crane operator needs the total rated load, in kilonewtons, for a lifting beam. The rating is 17 kN above the force needed to move 9 identical pallets at once, where that force is stated in kilonewtons. Each pallet's share is the force that accelerates one 124 kg pallet, less 6 N recovered by a counterweight. Each pallet is 1.2 m wide. The pallet's acceleration, in m/s², equals the greatest common divisor of 191 and 297. What is the rated load, in kN?
w10_P4_000837: A haulage contractor is reporting the grand total force, in newtons, that its winches must produce over a 9-day contract. Each day's requirement is 18 N above the force needed for 3 sites, each site pulling 7 identical loaded sledges at once. Every sledge has a mass of 180 kg. The sledges are accelerated at a rate, in m/s², equal to the sum of 2k - 1 for k from 1 to 8. What is the grand total force, in N?
w10_P4_000838: An airport baggage supervisor is asked for the total energy of motion, in kilojoules, of every bag moving across 11 carousels, each carrying 8 belts, each belt moving 2 identical bags. Each bag has a mass of 52 kg, and its energy of motion at belt speed is expressed in kilojoules. The belt speed, in m/s, equals the area under the curve y = 1·x² + 1·x from x = 0 to x = 1. What is the total energy of motion, in kJ?
w10_P4_000843: A maglev test facility is compiling the total energy of motion, in joules, delivered across 12 test days, each with 4 runs of the same test vehicle. The vehicle has a mass of 50 000 g. Its run speed, in m/s, is 5 times the area under the curve y = 1·x² + 8x from x = 1 to x = 2. What is the total energy of motion, in J, across all 12 days?
w10_P4_000845: A 6 000 g lab trolley rolls along a track at a speed, in m/s, equal to the smaller root of x² - 11x + 30 = 0. Its energy of motion at that speed is expressed in kilojoules. The lab repeats the run 3 times, and the energies of motion of the 3 runs are added together. A charging pad then adds 7 kJ to the trolley's battery, while the trolley's motor uses 8 kJ during the runs. What is the net energy balance, in kJ, after all this?
w10_P4_000856: A 37 kg robot arm moves at a speed, in m/s, equal to the greatest common divisor of 24 and 22. Its energy of motion at that speed is expressed in kilojoules. The arm's reach is 1.4 m. The arm makes 7 moves per part, handles 5 parts per hour, and runs for 5 hours. What is the total energy of motion, in kJ, over the 5 hours?
w10_P4_000862: An 11 kg drone frame is tested on a thrust stand. The stand's acceleration setting, in m/s², is found by taking the area under the curve y = 4x² + 7x from x = 1 to x = 3 and subtracting 28. The test room is at 40 % relative humidity. The engineers multiply the force needed to accelerate the frame by 5 for a safety factor, express the result in kilonewtons, and add a fixed 19 kN mounting reserve. What is the final rating, in kN?
